_comment: C6-8 正文英译 · browserbase-mcp（2026-10-31）。八维+mcp 三维+runs/unknowns/related/sources 全键非空。

axes.model_access:
**It needs an external model to run Stagehand** — on the hosted line Browserbase itself covers the LLM costs for Gemini
(the official README states the hosted version "provides the LLM costs for Gemini"); the self-hosted line requires your own
GEMINI_API_KEY (switch models with --modelName plus the matching key). It is a browser-automation-plus-model hybrid,
not a pure interface wrapper.
axes.runtime:
The current flagship is the **official hosted remote server** (https://mcp.browserbase.com/mcp, streamable-http);
the self-hosted line goes through npm (@browserbasehq/mcp 3.0.0, 2026-03-31) or cloning the GitHub repo.
**The GitHub repo browserbase/mcp-server-browserbase is archived** (API-verified archived=true,
3,397★, last push 2026-07-20) — the README top states plainly it is "no longer maintained, kept for historical purposes,
not representative of current production services"; the underlying Stagehand repo remains active (MIT 25,883★, pushed 2026-10-30).
axes.local_files:
Reads and writes no local files — the artifacts are page state and extraction results (text/structured data) inside a cloud browser session.
The self-hosted line runs on your machine, but the browser itself is still a Browserbase cloud session (BROWSERBASE_API_KEY required).
axes.background:
The browser session lives on Browserbase's cloud (start creates/reuses a session, end closes it); no local background process.
The session lifecycle is managed explicitly by tool calls, not persistent.
axes.tools:
**6 tools** (README wording; hosted and self-hosted share the same set): start (create/reuse a session) / end (close the session) /
navigate (go to a URL) / act (manipulate the page from a natural-language instruction) / observe (observe actionable elements) /
extract (extract page data per instruction). The act/observe/extract trio is driven by Stagehand's act-and-observe paradigm.
axes.context:
No server-side cross-session memory; the context is the current Browserbase browser session (start can reuse an existing one).
In-session page state is naturally continuous; nothing persists across sessions.
axes.permissions:
The hosted line needs a Browserbase account (API key + project id, configured in the client); the self-hosted line needs the
BROWSERBASE_API_KEY/BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID/GEMINI_API_KEY environment variables.
**act manipulates real web pages** (clicks/form filling) — gate the authorization boundary per target site; cloud session content
is retained on Browserbase's side, so sensitive flows need your own assessment.
axes.fit:
Fits: agents wanting "cloud browser + natural-language web driving" (no local browser to set up); the hosted line for easy onboarding
with the vendor covering LLM costs.
Not a fit: wanting an open-source auditable full implementation (the GitHub repo is archived; the current implementation is closed on the hosted side);
scenarios that only need local browser automation (Playwright MCP is more direct).

mcp.transport:
**streamable-http** (hosted https://mcp.browserbase.com/mcp, officially recommended) + **stdio**
(npx @browserbasehq/mcp self-hosted); the README states both STDIO and SHTTP transports are supported, recommending SHTTP via the hosted line.
Verified: repo README (fetched via GitHub API raw 2026-10-31) + the docs.browserbase.com MCP page (200 direct).
mcp.auth:
Browserbase account credentials (BROWSERBASE_API_KEY + BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID); the self-hosted line adds a model key
(GEMINI_API_KEY by default). The hosted endpoint measured 400 direct (exists, requires a proper MCP handshake and auth — not a dead link).
mcp.scope:
Read surface (navigate/observe/extract) + **web write surface (act clicks and fills forms)**; no local file write surface.
Cloud browser sessions can carry login state — gate the "touching things on a web page" boundary per the target site's authorization.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- Rate/session-duration/concurrency quotas on the hosted line (the docs have account-tier wording, not enumerated item by item; per D9 and snapshot discipline no numbers are recorded)
- The model list supported by the self-hosted line's --modelName switch and each provider's key requirements (the README gives only the mechanism)
- Retention period and compliance boundaries of cloud session content on Browserbase's side (the ToS surface was not verified item by item)
related: A browser-automation contrast: Playwright drives a local browser as a pure interface with no model; Browserbase is a cloud session plus Stagehand model-driving.
Both are official web-facing servers: Firecrawl leans "read" (search/fetch/crawl/monitor), Browserbase leans "manipulate pages".
